meaning: Postgres (42P01) cannot find a table with that name. The table either was never created in this project, is in a different schema, or the name differs in case or spelling.
causes: The AI builder wrote code for a table but the migration never ran on your Supabase project (common when Lovable/Bolt are connected to a different project than you think).
The table was created with quotes and capitals, e.g. "Profiles", but queried as profiles.
You are pointing at a different project, for example the dev URL in preview and prod URL in production.
The table is in another schema, not public.

steps.text: In Supabase Table Editor, check the table really exists in this project and note its exact name and schema.
List tables from SQL to see exact spelling and case.
steps.code:
select table_schema, table_name from information_schema.tables
where table_schema not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema') order by 1,2;

steps.text: If it is missing, run the CREATE TABLE migration in the SQL Editor (or ask your builder to re-apply it), then enable RLS and add policies.
If it exists with capitals, rename it to lowercase so the client and SQL agree.
steps.code: alter table public."Profiles" rename to profiles;

steps.text: Confirm VITE_SUPABASE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL in each environment points at the project that has the table.

prompt: My app errors with 'relation "public.<TABLE>" does not exist'. Check every migration and the Supabase client URL. Generate the missing CREATE TABLE migration for <TABLE> with the columns the code uses, lowercase snake_case names, row level security enabled, and policies so users can only access their own rows. List any code that references a table name with different casing.

faq.q: Why does it work in preview but not when published?
faq.a: Preview and production are often wired to different Supabase projects or env vars; the table exists in only one.

faq.q: Do I need to restart anything after creating the table?
faq.a: No for SQL errors. If the REST API then says 'Could not find the table in the schema cache', run NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
